pages.title: Keldminster Chapter Archive
pages.content:
KELDMINSTER CHAPTER ARCHIVE

The Chapter Archive holds historical documents, parish registers, and estates rolls relating to Keldminster Cathedral and its surrounding properties.

Address: The Treasury, Cathedral Yard, Keldminster, KM1 2EF.

Opening hours: Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays, 10.00 am to 4.00 pm. Closed on Mondays and Wednesdays for document conservation.

Notice: Please note that due to the one-way system recently introduced in the Cathedral Yard, delivery drivers for archive supplies should pull up in the bay outside St Jude's gate rather than idling outside the Treasury steps.

> Staff        archive.ke/staff
> Archives index        archive.ke/archives
> Staff catalogue (login)        archive.ke/catalogue

pages.title: Staff
pages.content:
STAFF

Ruth Dale, Chapter Archivist
Email: ruth.dale@archive.ke

Peter Gedge, Conservation Assistant

Mary Clout, Volunteer Indexer

A note from Ruth Dale:
Researchers are asked to give forty-eight hours' notice before visiting if they wish to inspect original vellum rolls. We have limited space in the small reading room, and I cannot always fetch rolls from the lower vault while answering the door. If you are looking for property deeds from after 1920, please note that these are held across the lane at the estates office, not here.

pages.title: Archives index
pages.content:
ARCHIVES INDEX

A selected list of parish, chapter, and civic holdings in the collection:

- Keldminster Market Roll, 1684 (MS 12/B). Scanned and transcribed for public viewing.
- Vestry minutes of St Jude-without-the-Walls, 1704-1840 (MS 18).
- Cathedral fabric accounts, stone repairs and glazing, 1740-1798 (MS 23).
- Chapter Procession Account, 1721 (MS 31). Transcribed in the restricted staff catalogue (staff login required).
- Tithe survey of North Garth, 1812 (MS 44).

Please note: Routine tenancy agreements, modern maintenance records, and Close repair registers are held by Chapter Estates Office, not here.

> Keldminster Market Roll, 1684        archive.ke/archives/market-roll-1684

pages.title: Keldminster Market Roll, 1684 (scan)
pages.content:
KELDMINSTER MARKET ROLL, 1684

Call number: MS 12/B
Format: Vellum roll, two membranes joined with flax.
Transcription of the head of the roll:

A true and exact listing of all tenants allotted standings and stalls in the High Market of Keldminster for the Feast of the Translation, anno domini 1684.

First: Master Thomas Vane, skinner, occupying the lower bench beside the ditch.
Item: Gabriel Cross, tallow-chandler, in the second place.
Item: Widow Crane, for herbs and dried roots.
Item: William Peake, glover, for his table.
Item: Roger Teasdale, ironmonger, occupying the uppermost bench beside the conduit.

Pencilled margin note by Revd A. Finch, 1888: The last tenant was named first on the roll. Stalls set in the customary reversal.

STAFF CATALOGUE - LOGIN

This page provides access to internal staff records, shelf catalogues, and restricted digital items.

Patrons and general visitors do not have access to this section. If you are conducting local history or family research, please consult the public archives index instead.

pages.title: Restricted: Chapter Procession Account, 1721
pages.content:
RESTRICTED: CHAPTER PROCESSION ACCOUNT, 1721

Call number: MS 31/R
Custody note: Transcript entered by Ruth Dale for internal reference. Original retained in Vault B due to iron-gall ink deterioration.

Transcription:

Expenses discharged by the Receiver for the midsummer rogation and progress through the liberties of Keldminster, 24 June 1721.

Paid to the carters for two teams of horses, twelve shillings.
Paid for tallow and pitch to dress the axles of the three timber wains, two shillings fourpence.
Paid to four youths bearing staves before the cattle, two shillings.

Order of the progress:
The rear wagon led the procession from the west gate to the market cross. The vergers and choir boys followed after the tail of the third team, as is observed.

pages.title: Keldminster Forum - old records?
pages.content:
Thread: old records?
[dave_k] Does anyone know where the older records for the town are kept now? Trying to look up an old lease from 1912.
[colinm] Ruth Dale at Keldminster Chapter Archive looks after them and is slow to answer email. You are better off going round to the gatehouse on a Tuesday morning.
[fmarsh] The diocesan material went over in 1983. Colin is right, Ruth has them in the south room but she has a large backlog from the summer.
[dave_k] Thanks, I will try the gatehouse.

pages.title: Keldminster Forum - chapter gutter repairs
pages.content:
Thread: chapter gutter repairs
[close_res] Tenants in Close Row want a date for repairs to a leaking shared gutter. Water is running straight down number 4.
[estatesoffice] We require the original 1924 roof layout before the stonemasons can quote. We are checking with the archive.
[colinm] Colin: Ruth, if you're looking for the old gutter plan in the staff catalogue, the sign-in uses your work email. When I set up the new accounts I had to put 'lanyard' in the starting password box for every one. People were supposed to change it afterwards.
[ruthd] Ruth: Thanks, Colin. I never did change mine, so I should still be able to get in. I'll look for the plan tomorrow.
[close_res] Please let us know when someone is actually coming out.

pages.title: Keldminster Forum - one-way signs on mill lane
pages.content:
Thread: one-way signs on mill lane
[brian_t] Drivers are asking where deliveries should stop under the new one-way system. The signs by the bridge don't leave room for a van.
[colinm] The dray turned round across the verge on Thursday because it couldn't pull up outside the bakehouse. It took ten minutes.
[ann_w] Council highways said loading is permitted on the left, but that blocks the bend entirely.
[brian_t] The laundry van gave up this morning and parked right down by the mill race instead.

pages.title: Keldminster Forum - post office closing at three
pages.content:
Thread: post office closing at three
[pat_m] The post office has shortened its weekday hours, leaving the afternoon collection unchanged. The counter now shuts at three.
[colinm] It makes it awkward for parcel drop-offs if you work until five. You have to carry them back the next morning.
[m_turner] Mr Patel said head office set the counter hours based on footfall, but the royal mail van still clears the box at five fifteen as usual.
[pat_m] Yes, the box is still cleared at quarter past five, but the doors are locked. So registered items have to wait until the next day.

pages.title: Keldminster Weekly
pages.content:
KELDMINSTER WEEKLY

News and notices for the cathedral district and borough.

SUMMER FETE DONATIONS
The fete committee needs unopened prizes by the Friday before the summer fete. Items should be handed in at the church hall between 10am and 4pm. Bins and tins must have seals intact. The committee cannot take used books or loose toys.

CLOSE ROW REPAIRS
Tenants in Close Row want a date for repairs to a leaking shared gutter. Rainwater has been entering brickwork near number 4 since the frost in February. The estates clerk took notes on Tuesday but no scaffold has been booked.

LOCAL HISTORY NOTE
The Chapter Lease Schedule of 1752 survives in the Chapter Estates Office. It lists properties let by the chapter and the rents due on them. The office will send a copy to anyone who files form E-3.

> Estates office forms        estates.ke/request
> Town forum discussion        forum.ke/forum/t/189

Contact: fiona.marsh@weekly.ke

pages.title: Chapter Estates Office
pages.content:
CHAPTER ESTATES OFFICE

The Estates Office manages the secular properties, tenancies, and historic land holdings of the Dean and Chapter of Keldminster. Enquiries regarding residential tenancies in the precinct and surrounding chapter streets may be lodged during standard office hours (Tuesdays and Thursdays, 10.00 to 15.30).

Notice: Maintenance works to the stone copings along St Jude Lane will begin on Monday. Scaffolding will occupy six feet of the roadway. Access for residents will be maintained throughout.

> Public minutes        estates.ke/records/minutes
> Request copies of records (form E-3)        estates.ke/request

pages.title: Public minutes
pages.content:
CHAPTER ESTATES OFFICE: EXTRACT OF PUBLIC MINUTES

Meeting of 14 May 1998.

1. Close Row guttering. Received a petition from eight tenants concerning water ingress between numbers 4 and 6. Mr Crane reported that cast iron brackets must be cast to match the original profile. Works scheduled for the first dry fortnight after Trinity.

2. North Gate allotment supply. Noted that the standpipe remains uncoupled. As the ground falls under district council jurisdiction, the surveyor will write again to the town clerk.

3. One-way traffic scheme. The new routing along Prior Street has caused delivery vans to unload across the precinct entrance. The bursar will mark a dedicated bay opposite the timber yard.

4. Precinct summer fete. Permission granted for four stalls on the gravel turn.

pages.title: Records request (form E-3)
pages.content:
RECORDS REQUEST (FORM E-3)

This form is for members of the public seeking certified extracts from the chapter estate ledgers, boundary rolls, or tenement surveys.

Certified copies of records are sent by email once the form is received. Applicants must state the exact title or shelf reference of the record required and give the specific reason for their search (e.g. conveyance, genealogy, boundary verification). Incomplete forms are not processed.

Please complete the electronic fields below.

records.title: Chapter Lease Schedule, 1752
records.content:
CHAPTER LEASE SCHEDULE, 1752

At a Chapter holden in the Treasury on the Feast of St Michael, 1752. Present: Dr Thomas Audley, Dean; Mr George Vane, Precentor; Mr Robert Chace, Receiver-General.

1. Tenement at North Bar. Let to William Peake, saddler, for twenty-one years. Yearly rent four pounds, two capons at Michaelmas, and the repair of seven yards of boundary wall.

2. The Mill Mead. Let to Widow Crane. Yearly rent six pounds. Right of cartway reserved to the bailiff on three named fasts.

3. Close Row parcels. Let to divers persons under the customary covenant. All watercourses to run through their ancient gutters without diversion.

In this book the closing leaf precedes the opening leaf.

Certified a true copy from the original Chapter ledger: Chapter Estates Office, Keldminster.

directives.task: Read at least three pages in the Reality Viewer.
directives.subject: Directive 14-1: orientation
directives.body:
Agent,

Before sending any traffic, read the material Desk 9 recovered in the Reality Viewer: Keldminster Chapter Archive, Keldminster Forum, Chapter Estates Office and Keldminster Weekly. Reading is passive and does not pass through the connection, so the local intelligence cannot detect it.

Use this stage to note the staff names, the arguments on the forum, and which offices hold which records. You will need those details later, and any message you send to ask for them will be logged on the connection.

This directive closes when you have read at least three pages.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

siteNames: Keldminster Chapter Archive, Keldminster Forum, Chapter Estates Office and Keldminster Weekly

directives.task: Find a seed fragment and save it to Files. Start with Keldminster Chapter Archive.
directives.subject: Directive 14-2: first fragment
directives.body:
Agent,

Desk 9's initial survey noted a scanned market roll on Keldminster Chapter Archive. In a reality of this age, the seed usually appears first in the oldest records the town holds. Look for a detail that is given more weight in the text than seems warranted.

When you locate the document, use the Save page function in the viewer. Saving writes a static copy to your local files which cannot be altered from the other side. Unsaved pages in the viewer remain on their system and can be changed at any time.

This directive closes when one of your saved documents holds a fragment.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Transmit the saved fragment from the HQ Console.
directives.subject: Directive 14-3: transmission
directives.body:
Agent,

Open the HQ Console, select the saved document, and transmit it. If the document contains a valid fragment, the console will report RESONANCE.

Do not transmit saved pages at random to test them. Every transmission passes outbound through the connection and increases the likelihood that the local intelligence will register our presence.

This directive closes when the console reports resonance.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Get into Keldminster Chapter Archive's restricted file (Chapter Procession Account, 1721) and transmit its fragment.
directives.subject: Directive 14-4: restricted holdings
directives.body:
Agent,

Keldminster Chapter Archive holds a restricted document (a scanned chapter account) which Desk 9 could index but not open. Accessing it requires a staff username and password.

The login page gives the format used for staff usernames. For the password, check the public pages first. Small institutions often give every new account the same starting password, and not everyone changes theirs. Someone will usually have complained about it in a public post.

Note that login submissions pass through the connection whether they succeed or fail. Confirm the credentials before you enter them so that you do not make repeated attempts.

This directive closes when you transmit a fragment from the restricted file.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Find out which record to request, file form E-3 with Chapter Estates Office, and transmit the fragment from the reply.
directives.subject: Directive 14-5: records request
directives.body:
Agent,

Older records at Chapter Estates Office are not held online, but copies are released on submission of form E-3. Desk 9 does not have the reference for the specific record required. Check Keldminster Weekly first, or contact a local resident who works with the holdings and give a plausible reason for the enquiry.

You will also need to state a reason for the request on form E-3 itself. Requests without one are less likely to be granted.

The office sends the requested record by email through the connection. If the reply is delayed, fails to arrive, or contains unexpected text, take that as an indication that the local intelligence is interfering with traffic.

This directive closes when you transmit a fragment from the reply.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

advisory.task: Flood at least one document in the Scanner.

advisory.body:

From this point on, any data reaching your terminal, including incoming mail and viewer pages you have not saved,may have been modified in transit. Before relying on any document, load it into the Scanner and flood it. Altered sections will visibly shake under the flood. Be aware that repeated floods degrade the sample and make the reading less reliable.

Agent,

Proceed with the reverse seed injection immediately. Waiting provides no operational advantage, and the local intelligence will continue to trace the connection whether or not you send further traffic.

hqMail.body:
Agent,

You have been assigned Reality 0x81B0, local name KELDMINSTER. Keldminster is a small cathedral town. The chapter owns half its streets. It has a council, an archive, a weekly paper and a public forum. Desk 9 estimates it at a little under two months old. The inhabitants (non-canonical) will report a longer history, as their memories have been generated to remain consistent with the local state.

Standard reconciliation procedure applies:

1. Locate fragments of the reality's seed. These appear as ordinary facts, distinguished by the property that nothing in the reality is able to change them.
2. Save each fragment to Files and transmit it from the HQ console. The console will report RESONANCE if the fragment is genuine.
3. When resonance is sufficient, the console will offer injection. Inject the reverse seed to complete reconciliation.

Your cover identity is J. Quayle (quayle.j@hedge.ke). Outgoing traffic on the connection uses this name unless otherwise configured. Reading material on the connection is passive and remains private.

The local intelligence (designation pending) has not yet detected the connection. Once it does, incoming records may be altered in transit. Your poison allocation is loaded in the Scanner. Use it sparingly, as the instability rebounds after each flood.

Form 77-R will be filed automatically at the close of the assignment. If you have not viewed the orientation film, a copy has been placed on your desktop by Training.

D. Okonkwo-Vance
Desk 14, Canonical Restoration

hqMail.subject: Reality poison: your allocation and the rebound
hqMail.body:
This notice is issued to all field agents at the start of an assignment.

The Scanner floods a reality's lesser processes for several seconds. During the flood, records altered by the local intelligence cannot hold their state and will visibly shake on screen. Statements that are false only because a resident believed or misreported them are part of the local state and will not shake. The Scanner does not detect false statements, only alteration.

Up to three documents may be held in the Scanner at a time.

Please note that the instability rebounds after use. A second flood shortly after the first draws increased attention from the local process and produces a less clear reading. Subsequent floods degrade the reading further.

Allocations

hqMail.subject: Choir: Wednesday rehearsals
hqMail.body:
The Corps choir meets on Wednesday evenings in the basement chapel from 18:00 to 19:30. All staff are welcome to attend and no prior choral experience is required. The choir sings without words, so no sheet music or preparation is needed. Drinking water is not provided in the chapel, so please bring your own if required.

Access to the basement on Wednesdays is via the east staircase only. Facilities have closed the west stairs for the remainder of the month while the steps are being counted.

M. Ibe, for the choir

updates.text: Please let us know as soon as you have it. The plaster in number 4 is already bubbling along the skirting.
Parish council members will discuss the Mill Lane traffic scheme on Thursday evening at the institute. Members of the public may attend.
The refuse lorry had to reverse back up the lane at ten. The driver said he would not bring the vehicle down again until the signs are sorted.
Ruth: The gatehouse telephone rang twice while I was locking the south room door. When I picked it up, there was only the dialling tone.
The estates office counter will close thirty minutes early on Wednesday for file sorting.
I spoke to Mr Patel when I bought the paper. He thinks the Saturday morning queue will simply be twice as long now.
The index list for the south room appears to have three entries rearranged since yesterday afternoon. The archive remains open as usual on Tuesday.
The stonemason has agreed to hold the provisional date for the scaffolding until Friday.
The Diocesan Gazette from that period often carried extracts of town indentures if the church was an adjoining party. I have the bound copy for that year if Ruth has not found the roll yet.
The forum list shows a post was saved here twenty minutes ago, but the screen stays empty when I refresh it.
The streetlamp near the bakehouse on Mill Lane is out again. The parish clerk has informed the district works team.
